items.title: Micron Just Dropped Tata Projects for L&T on Its $2.75 Billion Gujarat Plant
items.summary:
Micron has selected L&T to build phase two of its $2.75 billion semiconductor facility in Sanand, Gujarat, after reported delays and friction during phase one. Tata Projects built the first phase, while L&T will now lead construction; the Singapore-based design partner continues its role, and Turner International is expected to provide project consultancy. The decision places clean-room execution, government support and India's semiconductor ambitions under a sharper spotlight as the first approved mission project moves into its next stage. 

In this episode of Front Page, we break down the contractor switch, Micron's investment, the role of central and Gujarat government support, and why phase two matters for India's chip assembly and testing ecosystem. We also examine whether the change reflects normal growing pains or exposes a deeper execution challenge as more semiconductor projects move from approval to construction. 

Can India deliver the next wave at the required scale?

items.title: TCS Will Run as Many AI Agents as Employees Within 3 Years, Says Chandrasekaran
items.summary:
Tata Chairman N. Chandrasekaran is challenging the fear that artificial intelligence will leave Indian software companies behind. His argument is that enterprises still need decades of legacy data, systems integration and industry context before AI tools can deliver measurable value. TCS's reported $2.6 billion AI revenue, one-gigawatt data-centre platform and partnerships with OpenAI, Microsoft, AWS and Anthropic form the basis of a wider bet on enterprise technology. The opportunity, he argues, is to reduce the cost of intelligence across India. 

In this episode of Front Page, we examine Chandrasekaran's case, TCS's AI strategy, the rise of AI agents and the pressure visible in Nifty IT, hiring and service jobs. We connect Tata's chip, data-centre and software ambitions to India's wider AI infrastructure opportunity, while testing the gap between rising AI revenue and falling headcount. Can Indian IT convert this tension into durable growth?

items.title: Kaynes Semicon Bets on Global Deals to Beat India's Chip Subsidy Deadline
items.summary:
Kaynes Technology is moving beyond chip packaging and preparing a full-stack semiconductor push across wafer fabrication, compound semiconductors and equipment manufacturing. The plan depends on joint ventures, a 30% capital subsidy under the ₹1.27 lakh crore Semicon 2.0 scheme, and a possible dilution of promoter holding to fund its share. With Sanand in Gujarat as a key location, the move could reshape India's semiconductor pipeline, but the partnerships and application window are not yet finalised. 

In this episode of Front Page, we break down Kaynes' proposed expansion, its MEMS, gallium nitride, silicon photonics and chiplet ambitions, and the financing model behind the next phase. We also examine why global partners and government deadlines matter more than the headline ambition, and what the outcome could mean for India's semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem. 

Can Kaynes close the deals before the mid-August window closes?

items.title: How BharatGen is building India AI with NVIDIA Nemotron
items.summary:
BharatGen, a leading model builder under the IndiaAI Mission, is collaborating with NVIDIA to build India’s foundational AI infrastructure using a fully open model approach. By combining Indian datasets with the NVIDIA accelerated computing platform and Nemotron libraries, BharatGen is training multimodal models with up to one trillion parameters, tailored to India’s languages,  cultural nuances and local industries.

By releasing model weights, datasets, and training recipes on Hugging Face, BharatGen aims to enable developers, startups, and enterprises across India to fully customize and deploy open, state-of-the-art AI solutions.

items.title: Nandan Nilekani to Fix India's Exam System: NEET Leaks End Here? #Shorts
items.summary:
Nandan Nilekani, Infosys co-founder, will lead a high-powered task force on examination reforms after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a major push to strengthen India's exam system following the NEET controversy, paper leak concerns and other examination irregularities.

The task force will review the country's examination ecosystem and recommend ways to make exams more transparent, secure and technology-driven. It will also suggest structural and digital reforms for the National Testing Agency (NTA), which conducts several of India's biggest competitive entrance exams.

The government said the panel will help improve the credibility of the examination system, with further details on its members, timeline and recommendations expected to be announced separately.

Nandan Nilekani, Infosys co-founder, will lead a high-powered task force on examination reforms after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a major push to strengthen India's exam system following the NEET controversy, paper leak concerns and other examination irregularities.

The task force will review the country's examination ecosystem and recommend ways to make exams more transparent, secure and technology-driven. It will also suggest structural and digital reforms for the National Testing Agency (NTA), which conducts several of India's biggest competitive entrance exams.

The government said the panel will help improve the credibility of the examination system, with further details on its members, timeline and recommendations expected to be announced separately.
